evidence_registry.speaker: Charles
evidence_registry.text: I run a fair amount and my experience has been most runners are particular about the shoe brand and they've put some level of thought into - whether it's stability, fit, foot issues. Like, how do you think about getting people to break their habit of maybe, maybe they're a Brooks person or maybe they're whatever their brand, Hoka, whatever their brand of choice might be, those tend to be sticky. How do you think about breaking through with a new brand?

evidence_registry.speaker: Charles
evidence_registry.text: I really liked your answers and your enthusiasm for the category. I've been thinking about something you said that, that I can't seem to shake…

evidence_registry.speaker: Charles
evidence_registry.text: I think it's a consumer behavior mindset issue.

evidence_registry.speaker: Charles
evidence_registry.text: I was an early investor in Fitbit and Fitbit really never figured that part of the business out.

evidence_registry.speaker: Charles
evidence_registry.text: And my concern is that that's why we don't have a smart shoe yet.

evidence_registry.speaker: Charles
evidence_registry.text: And I think part of it is that I just worry that the consumer's not ready to think of a smart shoe as a - whether they're paying for the shoe, paying for the tech in the shoe, paying for access to the app.

evidence_registry.speaker: Charles
evidence_registry.text: I just worry that consumers aren't ready to pay for that bundle yet and that that will be an uphill challenge.

evidence_registry.speaker: Charles
evidence_registry.text: But that gives me too much pause to go forward now.

evidence_registry.speaker: Charles
evidence_registry.text: But I have to say that you, as a fellow runner I think you really are in tune with the community and I wish you nothing but success.

rationales.explanation: Charles asks how Avelo can overcome runners’ sticky brand preferences and established shoe habits.
Charles explicitly praises the founder’s answers.
Charles positively assesses the founder’s enthusiasm for the category.
Charles cites his experience as an early Fitbit investor and Fitbit’s failure to solve the analogous payment model as context for his concern.
Charles worries that consumers are not yet ready to adopt and pay for a smart-shoe bundle, making the category’s timing unfavorable.
Charles is concerned about consumer willingness to pay for the shoe, embedded technology, or app access, viewing the bundled monetization model as an uphill challenge.
Charles directly states that the payment challenge gives him too much pause to proceed with the investment.
